work: A Church in the House. A Sermon Concerning Family Religion
heading: A Church in the House

items.text: Maintain and keep up religion and the fear of God in your family, as one who must give account.
items.citation: A Church in the House
items.quote: maintain and keep up religion and the fear of God in their families, as those who must give account

work: A Church in the House. A Sermon Concerning Family Religion
heading: A Church in the House · Part I

items.text: Read the Scriptures to your household in a solemn manner, require their attendance and attention, and ask whether they understand what they hear.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: You must read the Scriptures to your families, in a solemn manner, requiring their attendance on your reading, and their attention to it; and inquiring sometimes whether they understand what you read.

items.text: Keep Bibles in your house and value them above your necessary food.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: It is better to be without bread in your houses than without Bibles, for the words of God's mouth are and should be to you more than your necessary food.

items.text: Catechise your children and make them learn a good catechism by heart, and help them understand it.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: You must also catechise your children and servants, so long as they continue in that age of life which needs this 'milk.'

items.text: Catechise your servants likewise, as long as they need such milk.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: You must also catechise your children and servants, so long as they continue in that age of life which needs this 'milk.'

items.text: Teach your children the things of God by talking of them as you sit in the house, walk by the way, lie down, and rise up.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: Teach your children the things of God, by talking of them as we sit in the house, and go by the way, when we lie down, and when we rise up.

items.text: Read other good books to your family for their instruction.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: the seasonable reading of other good books will contribute very much to family instruction.

work: A Church in the House. A Sermon Concerning Family Religion
heading: A Church in the House · Part III

items.text: Set up family worship in your house and lead your household in it.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part III
items.quote: Let those masters of families who have hitherto lived in the neglect of family religion be persuaded now to set it up

items.text: Teach them the good knowledge of the Lord and be their mouth to God in prayer, blessing them in the name of God.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part III
items.quote: teaches them the good knowledge of the Lord, and is their mouth to God in prayer, blessing them in the name of God

work: A Church in the House. A Sermon Concerning Family Religion
heading: A Church in the House · Part I

items.text: Consecrate your house and all in it to God, giving up every person and possession to his service.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: with ourselves we must give up our houses to the Lord, to be to him for a name and a people

items.text: Teach the truths of Christ to your household, as a prophet.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: keep up family doctrine

items.text: Lead the worship of God in your house, as a priest.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: keep up family worship

items.text: Administer discipline in your house, as a king, enforcing Christ's laws.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: keep up family discipline

items.text: Train up your children in the faith until they can take their place in the larger church.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: under the tuition of them, to be trained up till they become capable of a place and a name in particular churches

work: A Church in the House. A Sermon Concerning Family Religion
heading: A Church in the House · Part I

items.text: Lead the household in worship that acknowledges God as founder, owner, and ruler of the family, and honors Christ as its head and upholder.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I §1
items.quote: You ought to make family acknowledgments of your dependence upon God and his providence, as you are a family.

items.text: Lead the household in confessing sins committed in its family capacity and bewailing daily infirmities, to be reconciled to God and one another.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I §2
items.quote: You ought to make family confessions of your sins against God; those sins you have contracted the guilt of in your family capacity.

items.text: Lead the household in offering thanksgiving for common mercies: protection, health, provision, and the privileges of a Christian family.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I §3
items.quote: You ought to offer up family thanksgivings for the blessings which you, with your families, receive from God.

items.text: Lead the household in praying together for daily bread, wisdom for affairs, comfort, and sanctification of trials.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I §4
items.quote: You ought to present your family petitions for the mercy and grace which your families stand in need of.

work: A Church in the House. A Sermon Concerning Family Religion
heading: A Church in the House · Part I

items.text: Catechise your children and teach them the knowledge of God; you are their best teachers.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: parents are, or should be, their best teachers

items.text: Bring up your baptized children in the fear of God, as those dedicated to him.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: bring them up in that fear

items.text: Reprove, exhort, and encourage your children; pray with and for them, and set them a good example.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: reprove, exhort, and encourage tLem as there is occasion; if you pray with them, and for them, and set them a good example

items.text: Warn your children of the ways of sin, that you may deliver their souls and your own.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: Give them warning, that, if possible, you may deliver their souls

items.text: In disposing of your children, have first regard to their souls' welfare.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: consult their souls welfare in the disposal of them

items.text: Keep up family worship; go before your household in offering the spiritual sacrifices of prayer and praise.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: Keep up family worship... go before them, in offering the spiritual sacrifices of prayer and praise

items.text: In family prayer, dwell chiefly on the concerns of the family, that it may be truly a family prayer.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: ordinarily to dwell most upon the concerns of those who join in their family capacity

items.text: Command your children and all your household to keep the way of the Lord.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the Lord

work: A Church in the House. A Sermon Concerning Family Religion
heading: A Church in the House · Part II

items.text: Keep up religion in the house, that sin and Satan may not rule there.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part II
items.quote: the way to keep sin out of the house, is to keep up religion in the house

items.text: Conduct daily devotions and family worship, making your house a house of the Lord.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part II
items.quote: our daily devotion the sweetest of our daily delights, and our family worship the most valuable of our family comforts

items.text: Maintain constant prayer in the family, so that in sickness and death you may pray comfortably.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part II
items.quote: They who pray constantly when they are well, may pray comfortably when they are sick.

items.text: Leave your children a good inheritance by keeping up religion in the house, that they may rise up and call you blessed.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part II
items.quote: A family altar will be the best entail; your children will for this rise up and call you blessed

work: A Church in the House. A Sermon Concerning Family Religion
heading: A Church in the House · Part II

items.text: Pray with and for them daily, and leave them the benefit of many prayers stored up in heaven.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part II
items.quote: praying daily with and for their children

items.text: Leave them a good example of family religion that they may follow when they have households of their own.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part II
items.quote: leave your children a good example

items.text: Catechize them well and teach them the Holy Scriptures from childhood so public preaching profits them.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part II
items.quote: Let families be well catechised, and then the public preaching of the word will be the more profitable

items.text: Train them in the ways of God so that religion becomes a family inheritance handed down through generations.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part II
items.quote: make known the ways of God to our children, that they may arise and declare them to their children

items.text: Keep up family worship as a regular practice in your house, so that it may plead prescription.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part II
items.quote: family worship, besides all its other pleas for itself, be able in your houses to plead prescription

items.text: Second public reproofs and admonitions with your own family discipline, that they may be firmly fixed.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part II
items.quote: masters of families would second them with their family discipline

work: A Church in the House. A Sermon Concerning Family Religion
heading: A Church in the House · Part III

items.text: Conduct family worship daily: prayer, Bible reading, psalm singing, and catechizing; do not let worldly business crowd it out.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part III
items.quote: you will live no longer in the neglect of so great, and necessary, and comfortable a duty as this of family worship is

items.text: Catechize your children and have them repeat what they have learned, as part of family worship.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part III
items.quote: no repetition, no catechising

items.text: Call your servants to join the family worship; do not exclude them because they are busy with other work.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part III
items.quote: your servants are otherwise employed, and you think it is no matter for calling them in

items.text: If family worship has been left off, revive it: repent and return to your first works, cleansing the sanctuary and repairing the altar.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part III
items.quote: remember whence they are fallen, and repent, and do their first works

items.text: Do not perform family worship as a mere form; give it your best time and attention, with reverence and sincerity, not as a lifeless tale.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part III
items.quote: It is not enough that you do that which is good, but you must do it well.

work: A Church in the House. A Sermon Concerning Family Religion
heading: A Church in the House · Part II

items.text: Set up and keep up family worship in your house, that you and your household may give glory to God together.
items.citation: Church in the House, Part II
items.quote: set up and keep up for him a throne and an altar, that from the altar you and yours may give glory to him

items.text: Govern your household by God's law, making his word the rule for yourself and all in your house.
items.citation: Church in the House, Part II
items.quote: from the throne he may give law to you and yours

work: A Church in the House. A Sermon Concerning Family Religion
heading: A Church in the House · Part I

items.text: Pray with your children; let them hear you ask God's blessing on the instruction you give them.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: let them hear you pray to God for a blessing upon the good instructions and counsels you give them

items.text: Continue in prayer with your servants; do not deny them what is just and equal by omitting it.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: Masters do not give to their servants that which is just and equal if they do not continue in prayer with them.

items.text: Lead your family to pray together against the temptations to which families are exposed, such as worldliness, discord, and distrust.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: they should therefore not only watch, but pray together, that they be not overcome by the temptations they are exposed to.

items.text: Seek family blessings by joint prayer, for God commands blessing on families that dwell together in unity.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: These joint blessings must be sued out by joint prayers.

items.text: Make family intercessions for relations, neighbours, public authorities, and the church, and let your family join with you.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: You ought to make family intercessions for others also.

items.text: Sing psalms in your family as part of daily worship, teaching and admonishing one another.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: the singing of psalms in your families... to teach and admonish one another.

items.text: Use your parental authority to engage your children for God and godliness, encouraging what is good and discouraging what is evil.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: Countenance every thing that is good and praiseworthy in your children... Discountenance every thing that is evil in your children

items.text: Use your authority over your servants to engage them for God and godliness, encouraging good and rebuking evil.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: Countenance every thing that is good and praiseworthy in your servants... Discountenance every thing that is evil in your servants

items.text: Do not provoke your children to wrath, lest they be discouraged.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: be careful not to provoke your children to wrath, lest they be discouraged

items.text: Forbear or moderate threatening your servants.
items.citation: A Church in the House, Part I
items.quote: as to your servants, it is your duty to forbear, or moderate, threatening

work: A Church in the House. A Sermon Concerning Family Religion
heading: A Church in the House · Part III

items.text: Set a good example before your household, teaching them by your conduct to be meek, humble, sober, temperate, loving, peaceable, just, and honest.
items.citation: Henry, A Church in the House, Part III, 4
items.quote: Let the example you set your families be throughout good, and by it teach them to be meek and humble, sober and temperate.

items.text: Begin family worship as soon as you establish a household; do not put it off.
items.citation: Henry, A Church in the House, Part III, 5
items.quote: Let those who are setting out in the world set up a church in their house at first, and not defer it.

items.text: When you move, carry family worship with you; do not leave it behind.
items.citation: Henry, A Church in the House, Part III, 6
items.quote: In all your removals be sure you take the 'church in your house' along with you.

items.text: If you must be away from home, arrange that family worship still occurs and the household is not left neglected.
items.citation: Henry, A Church in the House, Part III, 6
items.quote: you ought to take care that the church in your house be not neglected when you are abroad

items.text: Attend family worship eagerly and attentively, counting it a privilege; do not discourage those who lead it.
items.citation: Henry, A Church in the House, Part III, 7
items.quote: Let the children of praying parents account it a great privilege to live in houses that have churches in them, and be careful to improve that privilege.

items.text: Be forward and attentive in family worship, making its exercises easy and pleasant for those who lead them.
items.citation: Henry, A Church in the House, Part III, 7
items.quote: make the religious exercises of your family easy and pleasant to those who perform them, by showing yourselves forward to attend on them
